Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An accordion type folding door system having a plurality of elongated panels hinged together along their longitudinal side edges into a pleated or zig zag arrangement, the folding panels being interconnected by a hinge assembly. The hinge assembly is disposed between and interconnects a pair of adjacent panels, each of the pair of interconnected adjacent panels including a side edge having longitudinal groove and an extension flange, wherein the hinge assembly includes a hinge pin and a plurality of hinge knuckles disposed vertically end-to-end in alternating arrangement on the hinge pin, the hinge knuckle having a tubular central opening for accepting the hinge pin, an outwardly extending tongue for connecting to a corresponding longitudinal groove in an adjacent panel in a tongue and groove connection, and an outwardly flared wedge that extends beyond the extension flanges of the panels, whereby the wedge cooperates with the extension flanges to limit angular folding extension to a maximum desired angle.

outputs.L1: An accordion-type folding door system includes a plurality of elongated panels hinged together along their longitudinal side edges in a pleated or zigzag arrangement. The folding panels are interconnected by a hinge assembly disposed between, and interconnecting, a pair of adjacent panels. Each of the pair of interconnected adjacent panels includes a side edge having a longitudinal groove and an extension flange. The hinge assembly includes a hinge pin and a plurality of hinge knuckles arranged vertically end-to-end in an alternating configuration on the hinge pin. Each hinge knuckle has a tubular central opening configured to receive the hinge pin, an outwardly extending tongue configured to connect to a corresponding longitudinal groove in an adjacent panel in a tongue-and-groove connection, and an outwardly flared wedge extending beyond the extension flanges of the panels, whereby the wedge cooperates with the extension flanges to limit angular folding extension to a maximum desired angle.
outputs.L2:
An accordion-style folding door assembly includes multiple long panels joined along their lengthwise side edges so that they form a pleated, zigzag configuration. The panels are connected to one another by hinge assemblies. Each hinge assembly is positioned between, and links together, two neighboring panels. Each of those adjacent panels has a side edge provided with a lengthwise groove and an extension flange.

The hinge assembly includes a hinge pin and several hinge knuckles arranged vertically end to end on the pin in an alternating pattern. Each hinge knuckle has a tubular central passage that receives the hinge pin, a projecting tongue that fits into the corresponding lengthwise groove of a neighboring panel to create a tongue-and-groove connection, and an outwardly widened wedge portion that projects past the panels’ extension flanges. The wedge works together with the extension flanges to restrict the folding movement, preventing the panels from opening beyond a predetermined maximum angle.
outputs.L3:
The described system is an accordion-type folding door constructed from a series of elongated panels connected to one another along their longitudinal side edges. The panels are arranged so that they can fold relative to each other, allowing the door to collapse compactly when opened and extend across an opening when closed.

Between each pair of adjacent folding panels is a hinge assembly that interconnects the panels and permits controlled pivoting movement. Each adjacent panel includes a longitudinal side edge formed with a groove and an extension flange. These features cooperate with the hinge assembly to provide both a secure mechanical connection and a limit on the relative movement of the panels.

The hinge assembly includes a hinge pin extending vertically along the length of the connection between the panels. Mounted on the hinge pin are multiple hinge knuckles arranged end-to-end in a vertical series. The hinge knuckles are positioned in an alternating pattern, with successive knuckles connected to opposite adjacent panels. This alternating arrangement allows the panels to pivot relative to one another about the common hinge pin.

Each hinge knuckle includes a tubular opening through which the hinge pin passes. In addition, each knuckle is provided with a tongue that fits into the longitudinal groove of one of the panels, forming a tongue-and-groove connection. This connection secures the hinge knuckle to the corresponding panel while allowing the hinge assembly to extend continuously along the panel edge.

Each hinge knuckle also includes a flared wedge portion. The wedge is positioned to cooperate with the extension flanges on the adjacent panels. As the panels are folded toward one another, the flared wedge contacts or approaches the flanges in a manner that restricts further movement. In this way, the wedge and flange arrangement limits the maximum folding angle between adjacent panels, helping to guide the folding action and prevent over-rotation.

Overall, the system provides a compact and reliable hinge structure for an accordion-style folding door. The combination of longitudinal grooves, extension flanges, alternating hinge knuckles, a common hinge pin, and angle-limiting wedge portions enables adjacent panels to be securely joined while still permitting controlled folding movement.
outputs.L4:
An accordion folding door system is formed from a series of elongated door panels arranged side by side and joined so that the panels can fold in a pleated or zigzag configuration. Each panel is connected to an adjacent panel by a hinge assembly that allows the panels to pivot relative to one another as the door is opened or closed. The hinge assembly includes alternating hinge knuckles carried by the neighboring panels, with the knuckles aligned along a common axis and secured together by a hinge pin. This construction provides a durable pivot connection extending along the length of the panels while permitting smooth folding movement.

The panels may include complementary tongue-and-groove formations along their adjoining edges. A tongue portion on one panel is received within a corresponding groove portion on the adjacent panel, helping to align the panels and stabilize the joint during movement. This interlocking relationship also improves the appearance and function of the door by reducing gaps between panels and maintaining consistent spacing as the door folds.

In addition to the hinge knuckles and tongue-and-groove connection, the hinge assembly includes outwardly flared wedge portions positioned near the connected panel edges. These wedges are shaped to cooperate with extension flanges formed on the panels. As the panels pivot away from one another during folding, the flared wedge surfaces eventually engage the extension flanges. This engagement acts as a mechanical stop that limits further angular movement between the panels.

By restricting the relative pivoting motion to a predetermined maximum angle, the wedge-and-flange arrangement helps control the folding pattern of the accordion door. The panels are prevented from overextending, twisting, or moving into positions that could place unnecessary stress on the hinge components. This improves the reliability of the door system and promotes smoother, more predictable operation.

The controlled angular limitation also enhances the structural function of the door when it is extended or partially folded. Because each hinge joint is constrained to a desired range of motion, the panels maintain proper alignment and spacing throughout use. The result is an accordion folding door system that combines flexible movement with improved stability, durability, and control.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may be small, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. When we say **“the book,”** we mean a particular book, not just any book. When we say **“the sun,”** we refer to the one sun we all know.

“The” gives clarity and direction to sentences. Without it, language can sound incomplete or confusing. For example, **“I went to store”** sounds unnatural, while **“I went to the store”** is clear and correct. This simple word helps connect ideas and makes communication smoother.

Although “the” is short, it appears constantly in English writing and speech. It shows that even the smallest words can have great importance. In many ways, **“the”** is a quiet but powerful part of everyday language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an accordion folding door hinge system with alternating hinge knuckles, a hinge pin, tongue-and-groove panel connections, and a wedge stop limiting the folding angle.
counterfactuals.output: An accordion folding door hinge system includes a plurality of door panels interconnected by hinge assemblies configured for alternating folding movement. Each hinge assembly includes first and second hinge leaves having alternating hinge knuckles aligned to define a pin-receiving passage, and a hinge pin extending through the passage to pivotably couple adjacent panels. The panels include complementary tongue-and-groove edge formations that align and stabilize the panels while permitting controlled relative rotation about the hinge pin. A wedge stop is positioned adjacent the hinge assembly and arranged to engage a corresponding stop surface on an adjacent panel or hinge component to limit the folding angle between the panels. The alternating knuckle arrangement distributes hinge loads along the panel height, while the tongue-and-groove connection resists lateral displacement and improves sealing and alignment. The wedge stop prevents over-folding and maintains a predetermined maximum angular relationship, thereby providing a compact, stable, and controlled accordion folding door assembly.

counterfactuals.output: A pleated folding door comprises a series of elongated, vertically oriented panels arranged side-by-side and joined along adjacent longitudinal edges by hinge assemblies that permit the panels to fold in alternating directions between an extended door-closing position and a compact stacked position. Each hinge assembly includes cooperating hinge leaves or knuckles secured to opposing edge portions of adjacent panels and connected by a hinge pin or flexible pivot member defining a vertical pivot axis, with complementary stop surfaces, interlocking shoulders, or abutment flanges formed on the hinge leaves and/or panel edges. As the panels pivot toward an open or closed limit, the stop surfaces engage one another before the hinge can rotate past its intended angular range, thereby preventing overextension, reverse bending, or strain on the pivot connection while maintaining proper pleated alignment of the panels. The hinge assembly may further include recessed mounting channels, resilient liners, or concealed fasteners to provide a smooth exterior appearance, distribute loads along the panel height, and ensure stable, repeatable folding movement of the door during use.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a zig-zag folding door hinge mechanism using vertically alternating knuckles on a pin, with wedge elements cooperating with panel flanges to limit angular travel.
counterfactuals.output:
A hinge mechanism for a zig-zag folding door assembly comprises a first hinge member adapted to be secured to a first door panel and a second hinge member adapted to be secured to an adjacent second door panel, the first and second door panels being arranged for relative pivotal movement about a generally vertical hinge axis. Each hinge member includes a mounting portion configured for attachment to a respective panel flange and a plurality of hinge knuckles projecting from the mounting portion toward the hinge axis.

The hinge knuckles of the first hinge member and the hinge knuckles of the second hinge member are disposed in vertically alternating, interdigitated relation, the respective knuckles having aligned axial bores receiving an elongate hinge pin extending substantially vertically therethrough. The hinge pin thereby connects the first and second hinge members while permitting relative angular displacement of the associated door panels between an extended condition and a folded condition characteristic of a zig-zag folding door.

At least one of the hinge members further includes an angular travel limiting formation comprising a wedge element positioned adjacent the hinge axis. The wedge element is arranged to cooperate with a corresponding flange surface, edge surface, or abutment portion of one of the door panels or of the opposite hinge member. Upon relative pivotal movement of the first and second door panels, the wedge element progressively approaches and thereafter engages the cooperating flange surface so as to define a predetermined terminal angular position. Engagement between the wedge element and the flange surface prevents further rotation beyond said terminal position, thereby limiting angular travel of the hinge mechanism.

In one embodiment, opposed wedge elements are provided on respective hinge members, each wedge element having an inclined stop face oriented to bear against a complementary panel flange when the adjacent door panels reach a selected included angle. The inclined stop faces are dimensioned and located to distribute stop loads into the panel flanges and to resist over-folding or reverse articulation of the door panels. The wedge elements may be integrally formed with the hinge leaves or knuckle-supporting portions, or may be secured thereto as separate stop members.

The vertically alternating knuckle arrangement maintains axial alignment of the hinge members along the hinge pin and provides distributed support along the height of the hinge. The cooperating wedge elements and panel flanges establish a mechanical stop independent of the hinge pin, whereby the hinge mechanism provides both pivotal support and positive limitation of angular movement for adjacent panels of a zig-zag folding door.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical description of an accordion type folding door system having multiple elongated panels hinged along their side edges, including details of the hinge pin, hinge knuckles, tongue-and-groove attachment, and angle-limiting wedge.
counterfactuals.output:
An accordion type folding door system comprises a plurality of elongated, generally vertical door panels arranged side-by-side and hingedly connected along adjacent longitudinal side edges so that the panels may fold in alternating directions between an extended door-closing condition and a compact, stacked or collapsed condition.

Each panel is preferably formed as an extruded or molded elongate member having opposed longitudinal side edges. Along each side edge is provided a hinge formation adapted to cooperate with a complementary hinge formation on the adjacent panel. The hinge formations include a series of spaced hinge knuckles defining aligned cylindrical pin-receiving passages. The knuckles on one panel are longitudinally offset relative to the knuckles on the adjacent panel so that, when the panels are assembled edge-to-edge, the knuckles interfit in an alternating manner and define a continuous hinge barrel.

A hinge pin extends longitudinally through the aligned passages of the interfitted hinge knuckles. The hinge pin may be a metal or polymeric rod extending substantially the full height of the panels, thereby providing a continuous pivot axis along the adjacent side edges. The pin retains the panels in hinged engagement while permitting relative angular movement about the hinge axis. End caps, stops, crimped portions, enlarged heads, or other retaining features may be provided to prevent axial withdrawal of the hinge pin during use.

The hinge knuckles may be integrally formed with or secured to the side edges of the panels. In one preferred construction, each hinge member includes a tongue portion received within a corresponding longitudinal groove formed in the side edge of a panel. The tongue-and-groove attachment provides a secure mechanical connection between the hinge member and the panel body. The tongue may include barbs, ribs, undercut shoulders, dovetail surfaces, adhesive-receiving channels, or interference-fit surfaces to resist withdrawal from the groove. The groove may extend substantially the full length of the panel so that the hinge member can be slidably inserted from an end of the panel or pressed into place during assembly.

To control folding movement, an angle-limiting wedge is provided adjacent the hinge region. The wedge may be formed integrally with one of the hinge members, with the panel side edge, or as a separate insert mounted between adjacent panels. The wedge projects toward a cooperating stop surface on the adjacent panel or hinge member. As the panels pivot relative to one another, the wedge engages the stop surface at a predetermined angular position, thereby limiting over-rotation of the panels. The wedge may be shaped to limit the included angle between adjacent panels to a desired maximum, such as approximately 90 degrees, 120 degrees, 135 degrees, or another selected angle depending on the folding geometry of the door.

In operation, alternating hinge axes allow successive panels to fold in opposite directions, producing the characteristic accordion action. The hinge pins provide durable pivot support, the interfitting hinge knuckles maintain alignment of adjacent panels, the tongue-and-groove connection secures the hinge assemblies to the panel edges without requiring exposed fasteners, and the angle-limiting wedges prevent excessive bending or reverse folding that could damage the hinge joints or interfere with smooth operation. The resulting structure is suitable for closets, room dividers, partitions, cabinet closures, and other applications requiring a compact folding closure.
